title: The Year of Delegations
hook: Tribe after tribe arrived in Madinah to meet him. Islam spread by visits, not by armies.

screens.text: **Tribe after tribe rode into Madinah to meet him.** Not to fight. To listen, ask questions, and decide for themselves. And one proud chief, brought in tied up, left in love.

**The year of visitors.** From 9 AH, delegations came to the Prophet ﷺ from across Arabia: Tamim, Tayy, 'Abd al-Qays, Banu Hanifah and many more. Many of them accepted Islam, IslamQA reports [IslamQA 11575].
bubbles: The Qur'an had described it: *"And you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes"* [Q 110:2, Saheeh Intl.].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- In 9 AH and after, delegations came from across Arabia (Tamim, Tayy, 'Abd al-Qays, Banu Hanifah and others), and many accepted Islam [IslamQA 11575] (single organisation; "IslamQA reports").
- Surah al-Nasr: "When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest, and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes, then exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord and ask forgiveness of Him" [Q 110:1–3].
- Thumamah ibn Uthal of Banu Hanifah was brought in by a cavalry party and tied to a pillar of the masjid. Three days the Prophet ﷺ asked what he had to say; Thumamah offered his life, gratitude or ransom; the Prophet ﷺ ordered him released. He bathed, returned, declared the shahada, and said the Prophet's face, religion and town had gone from most hated to most beloved. He had been heading for 'Umrah; the Prophet ﷺ congratulated him and told him to complete it [Bukhari 4372]. The hadith gives no date; don't place it in a specific year. (scholar question Q40)
- The Christian leaders of Najran asked for a trustworthy man to go with them; he sent Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, calling him the trustworthy one of this ummah (community) [Bukhari 4380].
- No compulsion in religion [Q 2:256]; Day 71 teaches it.

**Likely questions**
- *"Was Thumamah a prisoner of war? Is that allowed?"* Say plainly that capturing enemy fighters was normal in that time. The point here is how he was treated and that he was freed without ransom before he chose Islam [Bukhari 4372]. Detailed questions on captives go to the imam. (scholar question Q40)
- *"Why did the Najran leaders visit?"* They came to talk with him about religion. Bukhari 4380 mentions a proposed mutual-curse challenge (mubahalah) that didn't take place; keep to the trust part unless asked directly, then explain simply and respectfully. Reports that they prayed in his masjid are from the early biographies and weren't checked by our sources; leave them out.
- *"Is there really no compulsion in Islam?"* Yes [Q 2:256], and Day 71 covers it. Faith has to be chosen to be faith.
- *"How do I talk about Islam without pushing?"* Live it, answer honestly when asked, invite kindly [Q 16:125, Day 71], and leave guidance to Allah. Respect the other person's faith; never compare it to idolatry.

**Escalate:** detailed questions on captives (Q40); a convert facing hostility over their faith (mentor; safety rule if needed).

**Don't**
- Don't claim every tribe accepted Islam, or give numbers.
- Don't tell the mubahalah or Najran prayer reports on your own initiative.
- Don't encourage pressuring friends or family to convert.
